title: Why Large & Mid Cap Funds Look Promising Now: An Abakkus View
description: An Abakkus Mutual Fund study suggests Large & Mid Cap Funds are an attractive investment category currently. The study highlights improving corporate earnings.

faq.q: What is a Large & Mid Cap Fund?
faq.a: A Large & Mid Cap Fund is an equity mutual fund that, as per SEBI regulations, must invest a minimum of 35% of its assets in large-cap stocks and at least 35% in mid-cap stocks. This structure aims to combine the stability of large companies with the growth potential of mid-sized companies.

faq.q: How do Large & Mid Cap Funds differ from Multi-Cap Funds?
faq.a: The key difference lies in their mandatory allocation. Large & Mid Cap Funds must allocate at least 35% each to large-cap and mid-cap stocks. Multi-Cap Funds, on the other hand, are mandated to invest a minimum of 25% each in large-cap, mid-cap, and small-cap stocks, making them structurally more aggressive.

faq.q: Are Large & Mid Cap Funds suitable for conservative investors?
faq.a: While they offer more stability than pure mid-cap funds due to large-cap exposure, they are still equity funds and carry market risk. They are generally suitable for investors with a moderate to high-risk appetite and a long-term investment horizon (typically 5-7 years or more).

faq.q: What are the risks involved in these funds?
faq.a: Like all equity mutual funds, Large & Mid Cap Funds are subject to market volatility. While large-cap exposure provides some stability, mid-caps can experience sharper drawdowns and liquidity issues in certain market conditions. Fund manager risk and allocation risk are also factors to consider.

faq.q: How is taxation handled for Large & Mid Cap Funds?
faq.a: These funds are taxed as equity-oriented mutual funds. If units are held for more than 12 months, gains are considered Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and are taxed at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year. If held for 12 months or less, gains are Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) and are taxed at 15%. Dividends, if distributed, are added to your taxable income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab rate.

faq.q: What is the ideal investment horizon for Large & Mid Cap Funds?
faq.a: Given their equity exposure and growth orientation, Large & Mid Cap Funds are best suited for investors with a long-term investment horizon, typically 5 to 10 years or more, to fully realise their potential and ride out market fluctuations.
